data.name: Hyacinthus
data.gender_notes: Hyacinthus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Hyacinthus was a beautiful young man beloved by Apollo. When Hyacinthus died, Apollo caused the flower named after him to bloom from his blood. The name Hyacinthus carries the meaning “Flower of the sun” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hyacinthus usually hope their child will grow to embody flower of the sun and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Hyacinthus belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Flower of the sun.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hyacinthus total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: היאקינתוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם היאקינתוס נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'היאקינθος', שפירושה 'פרח יקר' או 'אלוהים זוכר'. השם מוזכר בתנ"ך כבן של המלך אמוט ואחיו של הנביא אלישע. הוא ידוע גם כדמות במיתולוגיה היוונית, אך השימוש בו כשם נוצרי הוא עקב המשמעות הרעיונית שלו.

in_greek.name: Υακίνθου
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Υακίνθου προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'υάκινθος', που σημαίνει 'λουλουδί' ή 'ο Θεός θυμάται'. Στο Χριστιανισμό, το όνομα συνδέεται με την έννοια της ανάμνησης του Θεού και της πνευματικής ανάπτυξης. Ο Υακίνθος ήταν επίσης ένα σύμβολο της θρησκευτικής πίστης και της πνευματικής αναζήτησης.

in_latin.name: Hyacinthus
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Hyacinthus is derived from the Greek word 'hyacinthos', meaning 'flower' or 'God remembers'. In Christian tradition, the name symbolizes spiritual growth and remembrance of God. The hyacinth flower itself represents faith, loyalty, and devotion.

in_english.name: Hyacinthus
in_english.meaning: God remembers, derived from the Greek flower name
in_english.long_meaning: The name Hyacinthus originates from the Greek word for 'hyacinth flower', symbolizing 'God remembers'. In Christian tradition, it represents spiritual remembrance and growth. The name has been used since ancient times, reflecting the cultural exchange between Greek and Christian civilizations. It's associated with loyalty, faith, and devotion.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hyacinthus carries with it the rich history of Greek mythology. It is a name steeped in tales of love, beauty, and the transformative power of nature. The legend of Hyacinthus is a remnant of the ancient world that continues to influence literature, art, and culture today.
data.spiritual_significance: Hyacinthus embodies the spiritual concepts of resilience and transformation. The story of his death and the blooming of the hyacinth flower from his blood represents the idea that even in the face of tragedy and loss, new life and beauty can emerge. It serves as a reminder of the transformative power of the divine and the enduring nature of the human spirit. In Christianity, this idea is reflected in the ressurection of Jesus Christ, who overcame death and brought new life to humanity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Hyacinthus is the name given to St. Hyacinth, a Polish friar who spread Christianity in Eastern Europe. The name is believed to symbolize his deep devotion and commitment to the faith, as the hyacinth flower is known for its vibrant and beautiful colors, representing the radiance of spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: According to Greek mythology, Hyacinthus was a beautiful youth beloved by Apollo and Zephyrus. Apollo was jealous of the affections of Zephyrus and in a fit of rage, caused a discus to be thrown with such force that it struck Hyacinthus on the temple, killing him. His blood was said to have formed the Hyacinth flower.

The name Hyacinthus was also borne by numerous early Christian saints, most notably Saint Hyacinth of Poland (1185-1257). He was a member of the Order of Canons Regular of the Lateran and is venerated as the patron saint of Poland.
